items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: It was in Zurich that I met a man who later became a great friend of mine, Johnny Simmen.

ctx.x: But the management were not sitting on their bunns and we were booked for some concert tours. We played the most important cities in France, playing to packed houses. The reception of the public was great, the applauses terrific, atomic wrote Louis Fritch from Strasbourg. Some jazz fans were following the band from town to town. We had little sleep and lots of drinks. I doubt that now such enthusiastic atmosphere could be recreated.

Besides France, we did concerts in Belgium, Switzerland and Germany. I had been through Switzerland a few times going to and coming back from India and Egypt, but this was the first time I was playing in Switzerland. It was in Zurich that I met a man who later became a great friend of mine, Johnny Simmen. He knew more American jazz musicians than I ever knew existed. And there were very few that he didn't have records of.

We were the first foreign musicians to play in Germany after the war and the public had been starving for some jazz music as played the way we did. Jazz had been forbidden in Germany by Hitler. Our first date was for the German radio in Wuppertal and the director of the jazz department was Dr. Dietrich Schulz-Köhn who was a jazz enthusiast that I had met in Paris before the war when I was with Willie Lewis. Neither of us had forgotten the meeting because we saw each other often during the week that he was in Paris.
